exercise.name: Dumbbell Split Jerk

reference.title: Dumbbell Split Jerk
reference.listing: Video; data sheet: body part Weightlifts, equipment Dumbbell, exercise type Strength
reference.note: Reference used only to identify the movement. No GymVisual media is stored here; this rig, model and animation are original.

exercise.mechanics: Compound (dip and explosive leg drive, overhead punch, split-stance catch)
exercise.laterality: Bilateral arms, split stance (right foot forward shown)

breathing.pattern: Breathe in and brace before the dip, hold through the drive and the catch, breathe out after the recovery.
breathing.cadence: Dip about 0.35 s, drive and split about 0.4 s

prescription.tempo: Controlled dip, explosive drive, stick the split
prescription.load: User-chosen dumbbells you can lock out overhead without pressing them out; stop while every rep stays crisp
prescription.progression: Learn the push press first, then the split; add load while the lockout stays solid

cues.text: Dumbbells on the shoulders, elbows forward, feet hip width.
Dip straight down a few inches, knees forward, trunk vertical.
Drive up hard through the whole foot, then split: front foot forward, back foot back, and punch the dumbbells up.
Land in the split with the arms locked: front shin near vertical, back knee soft, back heel up.
Hold the lockout, dumbbells over the shoulders.
Step the front foot back, then the back foot up, arms still locked.
Stand tall with the dumbbells overhead.
Lower the dumbbells under control to the shoulders.

mistakes.fix: Keep the trunk vertical; dip straight down.

mistakes.mistake: Pressing the dumbbells out instead of driving
mistakes.fix: Let the legs launch them; punch under rather than press up.

mistakes.mistake: Short split with the feet in line
mistakes.fix: Step the front foot forward and the back foot back, feet hip width apart side to side.
Lock the elbows as the feet land.

kinematics.peak: ≈24° at the bottom of the dip, trunk upright (≈6°)
kinematics.norm: A short, fast dip with an upright trunk; the dip (unweighting and braking) leads straight into the thrust (Soriano 2024)

kinematics.setup: Front foot 34 cm forward, back foot 50 cm back (ankle positions), back heel up
kinematics.peak: Front knee ≈61° flexion (≈119° included), back knee ≈47° (≈133° included)
kinematics.norm: Elite lunge-style jerk catch: front knee about 102 degrees and back knee about 143 degrees (included angles) at the end of the support phase (Liu 2024, barbell)

kinematics.peak: Elbows ≈14° overhead, dumbbells over the shoulders
kinematics.norm: Arms straight overhead, dumbbells over the shoulders (clinical opinion)

kinematics.peak: 0.4 s drive and split, 0.8 s hold, 1.0 s recovery, 1.3 s back to the shoulders
kinematics.norm: Barbell split jerk: about 0.25 s drive (Liu 2024); controlled lowering (clinical opinion)

sources.title: GymVisual #1170512, Dumbbell Split Jerk, video (movement reference)
Liu, He, Ye, Guo, Pan, Zhu & Meng 2024, comparative analysis of the kinematic characteristics of lunge-style and squat-style jerk techniques in elite weightlifters (Life 14(9):1086)
Soriano, Jimenez-Ormeno, Lake, McMahon, Gallo-Salazar, Mundy & Comfort 2024, kinetics and kinematics of the push press, push jerk, and split jerk (J Strength Cond Res 38(8):1359-1365)

cautions: Stop if sharp pain, numbness, tingling or giving-way occurs.
The dumbbell load is your choice: pick a weight you can move with the form shown for every rep.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
Fast lifts: learn the positions slowly with a light dumbbell first, keep the dumbbells close to the body and clear a space around you.
Shoulder pain overhead or limited overhead mobility: use the push press or a landmine press instead.
If a lockout fails, step out and let the dumbbells come down beside you, never over the head.
modify: Balance or knee issues: use the push press (feet stay planted).
Shorter split if the back knee or hip complains.
regressions: Split-stance hold with the dumbbells overhead.

muscleNotes.quads_r: Dip and drive the dumbbells up with the legs, then catch the split on the front leg.
muscleNotes.quads_l: Dip and drive the dumbbells up with the legs, then catch the split on the front leg.
muscleNotes.glute_max_r: Extend the hips in the drive; hold the split.
muscleNotes.glute_max_l: Extend the hips in the drive; hold the split.
muscleNotes.ant_deltoid_r: Punch the dumbbells up as the body drops into the split.
muscleNotes.ant_deltoid_l: Punch the dumbbells up as the body drops into the split.
muscleNotes.calves_r: Finish the drive on the balls of the feet.
muscleNotes.calves_l: Finish the drive on the balls of the feet.
muscleNotes.upper_traps_r: Shrug the shoulder blades up under the lockout.
muscleNotes.upper_traps_l: Shrug the shoulder blades up under the lockout.
muscleNotes.serratus_r: Rotates the shoulder blades up for the overhead lockout.
muscleNotes.serratus_l: Rotates the shoulder blades up for the overhead lockout.
muscleNotes.hamstrings_r: Work with the glutes in the drive and the split.
muscleNotes.hamstrings_l: Work with the glutes in the drive and the split.
muscleNotes.core: Brace for the dip: the trunk stays vertical so the drive goes straight up.
muscleNotes.glute_med_r: Keeps the pelvis level in the narrow split.
muscleNotes.glute_med_l: Keeps the pelvis level in the narrow split.
